data.gender_notes: Utvansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who comes after or descends from a great lineage, an heir or successor. The name Utvansh carries the meaning “Descendant, Heir” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Utvansh usually hope their child will grow to embody descendant, heir and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth in Hinduism. It signifies the continuation of one's lineage and spiritual legacy.
data.etymology: Utvansh belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Descendant, Heir.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Utvansh total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

This name instills a sense of pride and duty, as the individual is expected to uphold and carry forward the traditions and values of their family.

historical_references.reference: The Utvansh dynasty was a branch of the Yadavas, who ruled over the western parts of the Magadha Empire in ancient India during the 5th and 4th centuries BCE. They were considered to be the descendants of King Ushinara, the last king of the Haihayas. The Utvansh rulers were vassals of the Magadha emperors and enjoyed considerable autonomy in their territories. One of the most famous Utvansh rulers was Mahavira, the founder of Jainism.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Magadha Empire, Yadava dynasty, Utvansh branch, vassals, Jainism, founder: Mahavira

historical_references.reference: Another reference to the Utvansh dynasty can be found in the Mahabharata, an epic poem of ancient India, where the Utvansh king Prasenajit is mentioned as a powerful ruler who ruled over the kingdom of Kasi (present day Varanasi) during the Kurukshetra war. He played an important role in the war by providing troops and resources to the Pandava army led by Bhima.
historical_references.time_period: circa 3000 BCE (the date of the Mahabharata is uncertain)
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Mahabharata epic, powerful ruler, kingdom of Kasi, troops, resources, Pandava army
